Summary: Mother sent Father a screenshot of her work schedule.
Full Message: [screenshot of mothers work schedule]
Impact: Created scheduling uncertainty by sharing a work schedule without an accompanying discussion or proposed parenting plan. Placed Father in a reactive position without context for how the schedule would affect custody arrangements.

Summary: Mother sent Father a screenshot of a field trip permission slip and stated she had already signed and filled out the medical form.
Full Message: [screenshot of permission slip for field trip (no medical form)] I signed and filled out the medical form
Impact: Mother completed and submitted medical and permission documentation for the child's field trip without prior coordination with Father. Excluded Father from shared administrative decision-making regarding the child's school activity.

Summary: Father acknowledged receipt of the field trip permission slip and provided his own signed copy.
Full Message: [Screenshot of field trip permission slip] Received. Attached is the form I signed as well.
Impact: Father confirmed receipt and submitted his own signed permission slip, establishing a parallel record of parental involvement in the child's school activity.

Summary: Father notified Mother that despite her December 15 written confirmation, the children had not been returned after Christmas Eve celebrations and no communication had been received.
Full Message: It is now 9:56 PM on Christmas Eve. Despite your written confirmation on December 15 that the children would return to me after your Christmas Eve celebrations, the exchange has not occurred and you have provided no communication at all. A return at this hour without notice or communication is unreasonable. Advise when the children will be returned.
Impact: Mother's failure to return the children at the agreed time on Christmas Eve created uncertainty and disrupted the established holiday schedule. The complete absence of communication compounded the burden on Father, who was left without information on a major holiday.

Summary: Mother stated the children had just left and would arrive at Father's in approximately 30 minutes, noting it was her day and she did not feel she needed to rush.
Full Message: They just left. They'll be over at your house in about a half hour. We just finished a movie. It's Christmas Eve and you'll have them the rest of the week. Today was my day and I didn't think I needed to rush anything at any point
Impact: Mother's unilateral decision to extend parenting time past the agreed exchange time without prior notice denied Father the ability to plan a timely Christmas Eve with the children. Mother's stated justification reflects a disregard for the agreed schedule and Father's parenting time.

Summary: Mother sent a receipt for a scarf Abigail selected as a gift for Nikki while Christmas shopping with Mother and requested reimbursement from Father.
Full Message: [screenshot of receipt] This is the scarf Abigail picked out for Nikki when I took her Christmas shopping. You may reimburse me at your earliest convenience. Abigail asked to get this while with me as she wasn't going to be with you again until today.
Impact: Mother made a unilateral financial decision involving a child-selected gift during her parenting time and directed a reimbursement request to Father without prior discussion. Placed Father in a position of financial obligation for an expense incurred without his knowledge or consent.

Summary: Father objected to Mother conveying custody exchange instructions through the children rather than communicating directly, and reiterated that scheduling must be confirmed in writing between parents.
Full Message: The children are returning to you today based on instructions you gave them. This was neither discussed with me nor agreed to, and it was conveyed directly through the children by you. This continues to disregard the boundaries I've clearly and repeatedly communicated: that scheduling and exchange decisions are to be communicated directly between parents and confirmed in writing before being acted upon. Do not communicate scheduling or exchange instructions through the children again. Your ongoing use of the children as intermediaries in scheduling matters is inappropriate and has been repeatedly objected to.
Impact: Mother's use of the children as messengers for custody exchange logistics placed an inappropriate burden on the children and bypassed direct parental communication. Created confusion around the schedule and undermined established communication boundaries.

Summary: Father requested written confirmation of the date and time the children would be returned.
Full Message: Please confirm in writing the date and time the children will be returned.
Impact: Father's request for written confirmation reflects an ongoing need to establish basic scheduling predictability. The need for such a request indicates a pattern of insufficient advance communication regarding custody exchanges.

Summary: Mother confirmed the children would be returned Wednesday December 31st at 5:30 PM.
Full Message: Wednesday, December 31st at 5:30pm
Impact: Mother provided a return time only in response to Father's direct request rather than proactively. Continued a pattern of requiring Father to solicit basic scheduling information.

Summary: Father confirmed receipt of the agreed return time.
Full Message: Confirmed.
Impact: Father established written confirmation of the agreed exchange time, creating a documented record.

Summary: Mother proposed a multi-day schedule change based on what the children reportedly wanted, suggesting the children stay with Father on New Year's Day and return to Mother the following day.
Full Message: So what's the plan for the next few days? The kids wanted to stay with you today instead of coming here and then going back and forth over the next few days. So if you're ok with them staying with you today, then they will come to my house tomorrow and stay with me through Monday night and head back to you on Tuesday, January 6th after school.
Impact: Mother presented a schedule change as the children's stated preference, placing the children in the position of appearing to drive custody decisions. The proposal was made without advance notice or prior discussion, creating same-day scheduling pressure for Father.

Summary: Father flagged an inconsistency between Mother's proposed custody arrangement and her previously provided work schedule and asked for clarification.
Full Message: Based on the schedule you sent me, you are working tomorrow, Friday (1/2). Please clarify.
Impact: Father identified an inconsistency between Mother's proposed custody arrangement and her previously provided work schedule. Required Father to reconcile conflicting information before making a custody decision.

Summary: Mother confirmed the children could still stay at Father's home even though she had to work the next day.
Full Message: Yes, they can still stay here
Impact: Mother's ambiguous phrasing created potential for misunderstanding about which parent's home was being referenced. Continued a pattern of imprecise scheduling communication.

Summary: Father stated he was available and third-party care was unnecessary, and proposed a clear schedule consistent with Mother's earlier proposal.
Full Message: I'm available and third-party care is unnecessary. Consistent with your proposal, they can return to you on Saturday and back to me Tuesday after school.
Impact: Father established his availability to care for the children, eliminating any need for third-party supervision. Proposed a clear schedule consistent with Mother's own earlier proposal.

Summary: Mother reversed her earlier proposal and requested the children be returned to her that same day, with a return to Father the following evening before she went to work.
Full Message: Then I want them to be with me today, as it's my day off and they can return to you tomorrow at 5:30 before I head into work.
Impact: Mother's abrupt reversal of her own same-day proposal created scheduling instability and placed Father in a position of having to respond to a second last-minute change. Demonstrated inconsistency in communication that burdens both Father and the children.

Summary: Mother offered to pick up Abigail within 30 minutes or asked if Father would bring her to a meeting location.
Full Message: I can be over in 30 minutes to pick Abigail up unless you would like to bring her to meet me somewhere.
Impact: Mother escalated a proposed schedule change to an imminent pickup without Father's agreement, creating time pressure and implying consent that had not been given. Placed Father in a reactive position without opportunity for deliberate response.

Summary: Mother expressed frustration at the lack of response and stated she needed to make plans for the rest of the day.
Full Message: It would be nice if you could respond so I can make plans and be with my kids for the rest of the day, that is left
Impact: Mother applied emotional pressure to Father to respond to a schedule change he had not agreed to. Framed the situation in a manner that implied Father was withholding the children from her.

Summary: Father reiterated his prior response, declined the same-day schedule change, and noted third-party supervision was unnecessary given his availability.
Full Message: I've responded. Same-day schedule changes aren't reasonable, and third-party supervision isn't needed when I'm available.
Impact: Father maintained his position on the agreed schedule, resisting unilateral same-day changes. Reaffirmed his availability as the appropriate caregiver in lieu of third-party supervision.

Summary: Mother argued Father should have sent the children to her that morning and accused Father of denying her parenting time on her day off.
Full Message: If same day schedule changes aren't reasonable in your opinion, then you should've sent the kids over here this morning, as it's my day off. So are you saying you're denying me to see my kids on my day off?
Impact: Mother reframed her own same-day schedule proposal as Father's obligation, shifting responsibility for the situation onto Father. The accusation that Father was denying parenting time created a false narrative unsupported by the communication record.

Summary: Father declined to continue the exchange, restating that he had responded to and declined Mother's retroactive same-day changes.
Full Message: I responded to your proposed plans and declined your retroactive same-day changes. I'm not going to go back and forth.
Impact: Father documented his position and declined further unproductive escalation. Established a clear record of the sequence of events and his consistent responses to Mother's changing proposals.

Summary: Mother accused Father of being manipulative and of denying her time with the children when it was her parenting time.
Full Message: If you were opposed to any changes then you should've stuck to the plan and I would have the kids from this morning until tomorrow afternoon before I head to work. What you're doing is manipulative and denying me to see the kids when it's my time with them.
Impact: Mother's accusation introduced adversarial and emotionally charged language into a co-parenting communication exchange. Such language creates a hostile co-parenting environment and may negatively affect the emotional well-being of the children.

Summary: Mother notified Father she would pick up Abigail the following morning between 8:45 and 9:00 AM on her way home from work.
Full Message: I will be picking Abigail up on my way home from work tomorrow morning. 8:45-9am
Impact: Mother provided next-day notice of a morning pickup, creating minimal planning time for Father and Abigail. The framing as a statement rather than a request continued a pattern of unilateral scheduling.

Summary: Father acknowledged the pickup notice and informed Mother he had emailed a proposed January parenting schedule.
Full Message: Understood. I've emailed you a proposed January schedule for review
Impact: Father proactively provided a written proposed schedule for the month, demonstrating an effort to establish predictability and transparency in parenting arrangements.

Summary: Mother reported that Abigail could not find her winter jacket and believed it was at Father's home, requesting it be sent with Abigail for an upcoming ski trip.
Full Message: Abigail can't find her winter jacket from last year. She said it is at your house but she cannot find it. It is not at my house. Could you please take a look and send it with her next time she comes over here so she can be appropriately dressed when we go skiing. Thank you
Impact: The message indicates the child was involved in communicating information about the location of her belongings between households. Placed responsibility on Father to locate and transfer the item without advance coordination.

Summary: Father confirmed Abigail's jacket was at his home on its usual hook and would be sent with her on her next visit to Mother's home.
Full Message: Abigail's jacket is here, on the same jacket hook as always. I'll make sure it goes with her the next time she comes to your house.
Impact: Father resolved the item coordination issue promptly and clearly. Established that the jacket had a consistent known location at his home.

Summary: Mother notified Father of a shift swap that changed her February work schedule and presented a resulting parenting schedule as a notice rather than a proposal, while offering third-party supervision if Father had conflicts.
Full Message: Here is my notice: I was able to swap my February 3rd shift for February 6th, so I don't have to work the night before and after mediation. The new schedule therefore is me working February 4th, 5th and 6th. If you have any conflicts with this change, I am able to provide them with appropriate supervision during that time.
Impact: Mother unilaterally announced a revised February schedule without prior discussion or mutual agreement. The framing as a notice and the offer of third-party supervision excluded Father as an available and appropriate caregiver.

Summary: Father rejected the unilateral February schedule notice, stating parenting time required mutual agreement or court order, and confirmed his availability to care for the children without third-party supervision.
Full Message: There is no agreed February parenting schedule. Parenting time will occur only by mutual agreement or court order, not unilateral notice. I am available on those dates; third-party supervision is unnecessary.
Impact: Father's response documented his objection to the unilateral schedule assertion and his availability as a caregiver. Established that third-party supervision was unnecessary and that scheduling required mutual consent.

Summary: Mother informed Father the children would come to his house after school that day and announced a shift swap restructuring the following week's schedule without prior discussion.
Full Message: Kids are coming to your house after school today. Also, in an effort to make it less of a back and forth next week I was able to find someone to swap with me and am now working the 12th, 13th and 14th. That way the kids can stay with you from Monday after school till they come back to me after school on Thursday.
Impact: Mother announced a same-day custody transfer and a restructured week-ahead schedule without prior consultation. Continued a pattern of presenting schedule changes as facts rather than proposals, removing Father's ability to meaningfully participate in planning.

Summary: Father acknowledged the message, noted it constituted a unilateral schedule change, and stated he would accommodate it for the week without agreement or waiver of prior concerns.
Full Message: I have received your message. This constitutes a unilateral schedule change made without prior discussion or consultation and reflects an ongoing lack of predictability in the children's schedule. To avoid disruption for the children, I will accommodate this arrangement for this week. This accommodation is without agreement and without waiver of prior or ongoing concerns.
Impact: Father documented the ongoing pattern of unilateral scheduling while prioritizing the children's stability. His accommodation created a written record distinguishing voluntary flexibility from agreement or consent.

Summary: Mother requested permission to take the children skiing on a snow day with a later return time that afternoon or evening.
Full Message: Good morning, Because the kids have a snow day today and we got a good amount of fresh powder, is it ok if they take advantage of the great conditions and come skiing with me today and come back to you a little later this afternoon/evening?
Impact: Mother requested a same-day schedule modification with no specific return time proposed. Placed Father in the position of approving a change without clear parameters or ability to plan accordingly.

Summary: Father approved the request and asked Mother to provide a specific return time or at least a time range.
Full Message: That's fine. Please let me know a specific return time, or at least a time range, so I can plan accordingly.
Impact: Father's approval was conditional on receiving a defined return window, reflecting the need for basic scheduling specificity. Father appropriately requested parameters to allow him to manage his own schedule.

Summary: Mother proposed a return window of 5:30–6:30 PM and offered to text Father if they ran later.
Full Message: Thank you. How about between 5:30-6:30? If we run later than that, I'll text you?
Impact: Mother provided a return window and committed to notifying Father of any delay, establishing a basic communication agreement for the day.

Summary: Father confirmed the proposed return time range.
Full Message: That's fine
Impact: Father confirmed the return window, establishing a documented agreement for the day's exchange.

Summary: Mother informed Father she was calling the school to report Abigail absent because she was not feeling well and may have had a fever.
Full Message: I am calling the school. Forgot to mark Abbie absent. She's not feeling well and feels like she might have a fever
Impact: Mother notified Father of Abigail's illness and school absence the same morning after the fact. Father was not consulted in the decision to keep the child home or in the communication with the school.

Summary: Father noted that Abigail's school absence coincided with the boyfriend's birthday, the day of the first court appearance, and the day after Mother's birthday, raising a concern about the legitimacy of the absence.
Full Message: Abigail has been kept home from school and reported as sick, on your boyfriend's birthday, the day of our first appearance (where she was taken shopping an hour away), and the day after your birthday.
Impact: Father documented the timing of the child's absence relative to other significant events, raising a concern about whether the absence was genuinely health-related. Created a written record questioning the pattern of circumstances surrounding the child's school absence.

Summary: Mother sent her work schedule screenshot and proposed a detailed March through April parenting schedule via text.
Full Message: [mother sent screenshot of her work schedule] My recommendation is you get the kids March 1 at 5:30pm or whatever time Mathew gets out of work. I get them back 3/5 after school. Back to you after school 3/9. My house after school 3/12. Your house after school 3/19 until 3/26 I get them back after school. You're house after school 4/1, my house after school 4/3. You get them back after school 4/7. My house after school 4/10. They come back to you 4/12 in the afternoon and back to me 4/15 after school. You're house 4/20 after school and my house 4/23 after school.
Impact: Mother submitted a multi-month proposed schedule without prior discussion, presenting it as a recommendation rather than a mutual negotiation. The proposal referenced a minor child's (Mathew's) work schedule as a timing anchor, involving him in parental scheduling logistics without his direct input.

Summary: Mother retracted the end-of-March portion of her proposed schedule, noting she was aware Father would be away from March 21–26.
Full Message: Nevermind the end of March. I know you'll be away 3/21-3/26
Impact: Mother's partial retraction of the proposed schedule introduced ambiguity about which portions remained under consideration. Created uncertainty for the scheduling period leading up to Father's planned absence.

Summary: Father informed Mother he had sent his response to the March/April schedule proposal via email.
Full Message: I've sent my response to your March/April proposal via email.
Impact: Father directed substantive scheduling discussions to email, establishing a more formal and documentable communication channel.

Summary: Mother acknowledged Father's email and stated she would look it over and get back to him.
Full Message: Got it. I'll look it over and get back to you
Impact: Mother acknowledged Father's proposal without committing to a response timeline, leaving scheduling matters unresolved.

Summary: Mother indicated she was generally agreeable to some of Father's proposed schedule changes but wanted more parenting time in April.
Full Message: I finally had enough time to look over the schedule you proposed. I'm ok with some of the changes but I would like more time with them in April.
Impact: Mother's partial response left the schedule in an unresolved state, requiring further negotiation and delaying the establishment of a confirmed plan for the children.

Summary: Father informed Mother he had responded to her counter proposal via email.
Full Message: I've responded via email.
Impact: Father maintained written correspondence to document scheduling discussions, promoting a clear record of proposals and responses.

Summary: Mother acknowledged Father's email response.
Full Message: I responded
Impact: Brief acknowledgment left scheduling matters unresolved with no indication of timeline or agreement.

Summary: Mother clarified she accidentally called Father and had intended to forward his number to a third party named Dawn who had Abigail for a friend's birthday.
Full Message: Didn't mean to call you. I was going to forward your number to Dawn. She has Abbie for Grace's birthday
Impact: Mother arranged for a third party to have Abigail during what appeared to be Father's parenting time without notifying Father directly. Father was not informed of this arrangement until Mother accidentally called him, excluding him from a direct decision about his child's whereabouts.

Summary: Father noted the children had not arrived at the previously proposed 5:30 PM time and that he had learned of a schedule modification only through a third party rather than from Mother directly.
Full Message: On February 16 you stated, 'My recommendation is you get the kids March 1 at 5:30pm or whatever time Mathew gets out of work.' It is now 6:25 and neither of them are here. You did not inform me or communicate any change to that schedule. Instead I was contacted by a third party regarding a modification to my parenting time for Abbie. I've accommodated the change. Going forward, any schedule changes must be coordinated directly with me and with reasonable advance notice.
Impact: Mother's failure to communicate directly about the March 1 schedule change required Father to learn of a modification through a third party, excluding him from his own parenting time planning. Created documented uncertainty about the agreed exchange and placed the responsibility for approval on a third party rather than the co-parent.

Summary: Mother provided a lengthy explanation of the March 1 events, citing Father's silence on a schedule proposal, Abigail's mall trip, a third-party contact for extended time, and Mathew leaving without informing her of a delay.
Full Message: On February 21st, you responded to the proposed March/April parenting schedule stating, 'I'm away and will review and respond when I return.' As of March 1st, I had not received any further communication from you regarding that proposed schedule. When Abigail went to the mall with her friend for her birthday, the plan was for her to return to you at approximately 5:30 p.m., consistent with the previously proposed schedule based on my work hours. In the absence of any objection or alternative proposal from you, I proceeded under the assumption that this schedule was acceptable. At approximately 3:00 p.m. that afternoon, Dawn contacted you directly to request permission for Abigail to stay later than originally planned. You responded promptly and approved that change. Because you were contacted directly and gave permission, I did not send an additional message regarding that adjustment. Regarding Mathew, he left my home on Sunday to meet Bella, as he was not scheduled to work that day. When he left, I reminded him that he would be going to your home afterward. He did not inform me that he would be arriving later than the anticipated 5:30 p.m. time. As a result, I was not aware of any delay and was therefore unable to notify you of a change. Additionally, the March/April schedule has not yet been formally confirmed or agreed upon. To avoid future misunderstandings, I am requesting that we confirm the March and April parenting schedule in writing. Please either confirm your agreement with the previously proposed schedule or provide any revisions you would like to suggest. A timely response would be appreciated so that expectations are clear for everyone involved.
Impact: Mother's explanation placed partial responsibility for the late exchange on Father's silence and on Mathew's actions, without acknowledging her own obligation to directly communicate schedule changes. The involvement of Mathew in managing his own travel logistics created ambiguity and placed an undue burden on the child to coordinate his own custody exchange.

Summary: Father addressed Mother's explanation, noting neither child arrived until 8:20 PM and that it was her responsibility as the exchanging parent to ensure timely arrival or notify him of any delay.
Full Message: My February 21 email stated I would review and respond to your counter proposal when I returned. In your early morning text today, you state that the plan was for them to return at 5:30 p.m. Neither child arrived until 8:20 p.m., and I received no direct communication from you requesting a change. As the parent responsible for the exchange that day, it's your responsibility to ensure arrival at the agreed time or, at a minimum, to notify of any delay.
Impact: Father documented the nearly three-hour delay in the children's return and established on the record that no direct communication was received regarding any change. Clarified the expectation of parental responsibility for exchange communication and coordination.

Summary: Mother informed Father that Abigail had asked to take the bus home with a friend and that Mother had written a note but could not make the decision herself, directing Abigail to ask Father.
Full Message: Abigail asked to take the bus home with Grace this afternoon. I wrote her a note in case you allowed it, as I can't make that decision. I told her to ask you, since she needed to figure out how she was going to get back to your house
Impact: While Mother appropriately deferred the decision to Father, the arrangement required Abigail to serve as the messenger for a logistical coordination matter between parents. Placed the responsibility on the child to manage her own after-school transportation planning.

Summary: Father acknowledged Mother's message about Abigail's bus request.
Full Message: Got it
Impact: Father acknowledged the communication. The brief response left Abigail's transportation arrangement unconfirmed at the time of the message.

Summary: Father relayed Abigail's request to stay at his home Thursday night and return to Mother Friday after school, and asked whether that worked for Mother.
Full Message: Abigail asked if she could stay here Thursday night and return to you Friday after school. Let me know if that works.
Impact: Father communicated Abigail's preference directly to Mother while seeking mutual agreement before acting on the request. Maintained appropriate parental communication channels rather than acting unilaterally.

Summary: Mother approved Abigail's request to stay at Father's home Thursday night.
Full Message: Ok
Impact: Mother approved the schedule adjustment, enabling a mutually agreed modification to the parenting schedule.

Summary: Mother requested a swap of her April vacation week parenting time, asking for the second half instead of the first half, citing newly available PTO and plans to take the children somewhere for a few days.
Full Message: I would like to run a change by you for the end of April. I've been offered to take some PTO and seeing that we have court on the 27th I was wondering if I could take the kids the second half of vacation week rather than the first half, as I was going to try and take them somewhere for a couple of days. It would look like this: Transition to your house after school 4/24 and transition back to me 4/29 at 3pm. Then they would come back to you after school on Monday 5/4 I understand if you would rather not make this change. Thank you for considering.
Impact: Mother's request to modify an already-finalized April schedule introduced new scheduling uncertainty after a lengthy negotiation process. The mention of a pending court date as context created implicit pressure around the timing and framing of the request.

Summary: Father declined Mother's request to modify the April schedule, citing the recent extended negotiation required to finalize it.
Full Message: I understand your request, but it just took us a month to even agree and finalize the April schedule. I'm not going to change it again.
Impact: Father's response documented his reasonable basis for declining a further schedule modification and protected the stability of the agreed plan for the children.

Summary: Mother elaborated on her PTO request, explained the circumstances that made the change necessary, and noted she needed to confirm with her employer by that evening or the time off would be offered to another employee.
Full Message: I had been hoping to plan a special activity with the kids during their April vacation. Until last night, I was unable to request that week off from work because the time had been previously allocated to another nurse. If you already have plans with the children for that week, I completely understand and do not wish to interfere. However, if there are no specific plans in place and the only concern is the change in scheduling, I respectfully ask that personal disagreements be set aside so the children can have the opportunity to spend quality time and enjoy a special experience on their vacation. I need to confirm my availability with my employer by tonight, as the time off will otherwise be offered to another employee.
Impact: Mother imposed a same-day decision deadline on Father regarding a schedule modification that had already been declined, creating pressure to reverse a documented agreement. The framing of Father's position as personal disagreement introduced an emotional appeal that minimized the practical disruption caused by repeated schedule changes.

Summary: Father asked Mother whether the children would be going to school that day and if not why.
Full Message: Will the children be going to school today and if not why?
Impact: Father's inquiry reflects a lack of advance communication from Mother regarding school attendance decisions. Required Father to seek basic information about the children's whereabouts on a school day.

Summary: Mother informed Father the children were not going to school because she was taking them skiing, describing it as a mental health day.
Full Message: No. They are not. I'm keeping them home because I'm taking them skiing. Mental health day
Impact: Mother unilaterally decided to keep the children out of school for a recreational outing without prior consultation with Father. The characterization of a ski trip as a mental health day introduced a potentially misleading description of the reason for the absence.

Summary: Father asked whether there was a reason he had not been informed in advance about the children being kept home from school.
Full Message: Is there a reason i wasnt informed?
Impact: Father's question documented his exclusion from a decision directly affecting the children's school attendance. Highlighted the ongoing pattern of unilateral decision-making without parental notification or consultation.
